unexpected_findings.summary: Stale-tab double migration lands a choice on a DIFFERENT word, and the notice says 'on the same characters'. The old Library code (analysis.71b110b249.js) is deliberately kept for 30 days (library/code/generations.json: retain_days 30, retired 2026-10-14). That old code's 'Apply interpretation' saves {declarations: v} (main analysis.js:1637), which drops token_cut, renumbered, undecided and legacy_declarations. The new page then reads those v2 numbers as v1 and moves them again. On 'Oh--oh, oh, oh my love' the user's choice (v1 token 2 = chars 8-10, migrated to v2 token 3) came back as token 4 = chars 12-14 and was SENT that way. Only a role=status notice appeared, and it claims 'moved … on the same characters'. A choice the old code picks from v2 evidence and saves unmarked takes the same path. Where the old number names a different word it blocks visibly (e.g. on 'Oh--oh, oh my love'), and the original v1 legacy copy is lost. Policy item 6 accepts unmarked = legacy, but this breaks 'never silently land on a different word', and the notice text is false here. Possible mitigation (not implemented): keep the mark or a fingerprint of the last v2-written declarations in a key the old code does not overwrite.
